Karthik / team,

Quick infra reality check after peeking at the curves:
- Baseline footprint requested ~8x A100-equivalent slots during peak windows. Current committed Dedicated reservations for Q3 already include two enterprise customers (one large banking customer + one AI video vendor) that consume roughly ~60% of our planned pool in us-west-2.
- We have ~25% headroom in dedicated pool if we accept ~15% latency degradation via denser batching and modest queueing.
- Burst capacity (on-demand) is available but it's constrained during weekdays 08:00-18:00 PST due to training/backfill jobs in our partner clusters; relying on burst for a strict SLA is risky.

Options to propose:
A) Reserve full dedicated commit for OrbitAI: requires reshuffling other customers (ask banking customer to move some planned jobs to off-peak) or expanding Dedicated fleet earlier than planned (2-3 week procurement + provisioning lead).
B) Hybrid commit: Reserve 60% of requested baseline + guaranteed burst credits for the rest with a contractual preemption policy (revenue-weighted preempt). This lets us avoid urgent hardware procurement but requires clear SLOs for preemption windows.
C) Prioritized routing to a quantized variant of the same model (lower cost/latency but slightly reduced quality) during high contention; would be acceptable for 2 of OrbitAI's pilot customers by their own admission.

If we have to prioritize between customers, my operational recommendation is: contractual SLA > revenue-weighted priority > fair-share. SLA-backed customers must keep their allocation. For non-SLA, we can apply revenue-weighted preemption credits.

I'll run a quick simulated schedule tonight to see the exact days we can accommodate OrbitAI without extra hardware.
